3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: I was walking to my office, since today was the day to edit and make the final changes for the proposal to change the Constitution of Sordland.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: Not long after, Petr, Lucian and Nia arrived.

7.speaker: Narrator
7.text: I walked in the marble corridors of the Palace, thinking about the huge decisions I was going to take.

8.speaker: Narrator
8.text: At the entrance to my office, my secretary Livia greeted me.

10.speaker: Petr Vectern
10.text: "Good morning! Time to finally get this proposal going."

11.speaker: Narrator
11.text: The reform committee finally bore tangible results and the draft of the changes were about to be presented to me.

18.speaker: Player
18.text: “I'm about to make stressful decisions. So, not feeling that great.”

20.speaker: Player
20.text: “I feel better now that I've seen you, Livia."

21.speaker: Narrator
21.text: She averted her eyes away from me and smiled.

25.speaker: Player
25.text: “You'll find out with the rest of Sordland, sweetheart."

29.speaker: Narrator
29.text: Livia left to hang up my coat. I entered my office and sat down.

31.speaker: Narrator
31.text: Petr placed the draft in front of me.

32.speaker: Lucian Galade
32.text: "After your modifications, we will be starting the process."

33.speaker: Narrator
33.text: After placing the committee's report and my own notes in front of me, I buried myself in the papers.

34.speaker: Nia Morgna
34.text: "I have suggested to bring some limitations to decrees regarding their applicability. While we keep them, we should try to make sure that they will only be used in emergency situations."

35.speaker: Player
35.text: "Regardless of him, I see no problem with having a special title for great heroes."

37.speaker: Nia Morgna
37.text: "Mr. President. Unless you wish to be like Colonel Soll after all."

38.speaker: Lucian Galade
38.text: "We could start talking about Section 3. This is about the impeachment process of the President. Currently, in cases of high treason and breaking the Constitution, the Supreme Court may impeach and try the President."

39.speaker: Player
39.text: "After pushing aggressive changes, I may need the same immunity."

40.speaker: Player
40.text: "If our own democracy is the reason of our downfall, we will have to accept it."

41.speaker: Player
41.text: "It's not unfair that former Presidents get some special treatment."

42.speaker: Petr Vectern
42.text: "It is a matter of both when we have the Communist Party and the Workers Party of Bludia getting more than five percent vote in the last elections."

43.speaker: Petr Vectern
43.text: "Well, regardless of what Mr. Rayne decides, we will need to work together to push this agenda."

44.speaker: Nia Morgna
44.text: "Most reformists want the impeachment to be initiated by the Assembly. They think they do not have any power over potential rogue presidents that would abuse their power."

45.speaker: Petr Vectern
45.text: "Don't forget that the Communist Party and the Workers Party of Bludia both had close to ten percent vote in the last election."

46.speaker: Nia Morgna
46.text: "You're right. Even after Soll's resignation, we still have three parties in the Assembly. Even Mr. Kibener's NFP was barely elected."

47.speaker: Player
47.text: "The Assembly should have oversight over the President."

48.speaker: Player
48.text: "Not sure if it is correct to chastise the President this much though."

50.speaker: Nia Morgna
50.text: "That would be enough to hold him accountable for his actions but why would you want to keep such a title, Mr. President?"

51.speaker: Nia Morgna
51.text: "The reformists would be completely behind that."

52.speaker: Nia Morgna
52.text: "I agree. Even after Soll's resignation, we still have three parties in the Assembly. Even Mr. Kibener's NFP is barely elected."

53.speaker: Nia Morgna
53.text: "Do you want to protect Tarquin Soll, Mr. President?"

54.speaker: Player
54.text: "Yes, he is a hero for Sordland."

55.speaker: Petr Vectern
55.text: "This law is particularly dangerous for you in this case. We will be going against the Old Guard, and if we prove to be successful in the Assembly..."

56.speaker: Petr Vectern
56.text: "Decreasing the threshold might mean opening their way into the Assembly."

58.speaker: Player
58.text: "I agree, we should abolish this position."

59.speaker: Petr Vectern
59.text: "You would be opening their way into the parliament in the future if you were to decrease the threshold. It is important that you realize this."

60.speaker: Player
60.text: "We should define a better impeachment process."

61.speaker: Nia Morgna
61.text: "I think this is a national matter, Mr. Rayne. Not a partisan one."

62.speaker: Player
62.text: "No, I think we should respect this law."

63.speaker: Player
63.text: "We could keep the title but take away the immunity clause."

64.speaker: Player
64.text: "Every President should gain that title after their term."

65.speaker: Player
65.text: "Maybe reforms are not a great idea after all."

66.speaker: Nia Morgna
66.text: "Many Sordish citizens feel they're not represented in the Assembly. This is a matter of representative democracy in Sordland."

67.speaker: Player
67.text: "What if we don't succeed? The Court can have me impeached for this."

68.speaker: Petr Vectern
68.text: "...They will be looking for anything they can declare unconstitutional to tackle you. All they need is the Supreme Court to impeach you."

69.speaker: Nia Morgna
69.text: "We must get rid of this senseless law that protects him. He should be able to face justice for the atrocities that had taken place during his rule."

70.speaker: Lucian Galade
70.text: "Of course that would also mean that USP might lose its majority in the Assembly, sir."

71.speaker: Petr Vectern
71.text: "That's why only Tarquin Soll has that title. He gave it to himself right after his military coup. This law is basically made to save the Colonel and it has a symbolic importance for Sordland because of it."

72.speaker: Lucian Galade
72.text: "According to the Constitution, the Member of Honor not only has legal immunity but the state also covers most of their expenses as well as providing security at all times. It can only be given to someone by an absolute majority vote in the Assembly and the approval of the President."

73.speaker: Nia Morgna
73.text: "Mr. Ricter and his PFJP definitely wants to see change on this topic. They find our 10% threshold to be antidemocratic. Which is something I also agree with."

74.speaker: Lucian Galade
74.text: "And the last one is the question about Soll's legacy. Basically his *Member of Honor* law. It gave him absolute immunity even when he's retired. He is a permanent member of the Assembly as well, but luckily he doesn't really attend anymore."

77.speaker: Player
77.text: "I may need to think a bit longer about this."

78.speaker: Nia Morgna
78.text: "While I do not have strong opinions about this point, these reforms are vital for the future of our democracy, Mr. President."

79.speaker: Petr Vectern
79.text: "But it would be tougher to persuade the judges with this. Mrs. Edmonds may not want to cooperate with you if they believe you're going to get rid of them afterwards."

80.speaker: Lucian Galade
80.text: "Yes, they are already trying to hit you since they are aware about the current wind of change. But we aim to cooperate with some of the judges to make sure that doesn't happen."

81.speaker: Nia Morgna
81.text: "Yes, we will be collaboratively working on the specifics."

82.speaker: Lucian Galade
82.text: "That is a better strategy. We'll need to sway some of their members to succeed after all."

84.speaker: Nia Morgna
84.text: "That might be the best thing to do for now. If we agitate the Court further, we might lose our chances with Mrs. Edmonds as well."

87.speaker: Player
87.text: "They should be able to be impeached. Why do I get to be impeached but not them?"

88.speaker: Player
88.text: "We should crush the Old Guards to clear ways for further reforms."

89.speaker: Player
89.text: "Maybe we shouldn't make the Supreme Court our enemies just yet."

90.speaker: Player
90.text: "We can't allow communists to enter the Assembly."

91.speaker: Lucian Galade
91.text: "I don't think that's a wise idea to include in the reforms."

92.speaker: Player
92.text: "We can't just give away our majority like that."

93.speaker: Nia Morgna
93.text: "We will make sure the Old Guards won't control the Court any longer, Mr. President."

94.speaker: Petr Vectern
94.text: "Well, they need absolute immunity in theory. But look at what reality got us? We've got to deal with the most corrupt Chief Justice in the world, with no chance to deal with him!"

95.speaker: Lucian Galade
95.text: "Section 6. This is about the presidential decrees. Reformists demand more limitations to the President's executive powers. Mr. Ricter has demanded them to be completely removed."

97.speaker: Player
97.text: "Don't worry. With these reforms, we will be even more popular."

98.speaker: Player
98.text: "We'll work with the reformists to limit the use of decrees."

99.speaker: Player
99.text: "But the high threshold is the reason why Sordish politics has become so isolated."

100.speaker: Nia Morgna
100.text: "While I agree that the current court members are *problematic*, this is no way to resolve it. The law is supposed to ensure the judiciary's independence by giving legal protection so they can't be pressured."

101.speaker: Player
101.text: "We should definitely work to decrease the threshold for better representation."

102.speaker: Nia Morgna
102.text: "I do not support taking away their power for yourself, Mr. President. The judiciary must be independent and long-lasting."

104.speaker: Lucian Galade
104.text: "It's the question about the immunity of the Judges. While the Anti-Old Guard sentiment is increasing, there are talks that taking away their immunity would give us authority over judiciary."

105.speaker: Lucian Galade
105.text: "Now I'll move unto the 8th Section. We are reaching the end."

106.speaker: Player
106.text: "Do you think it would really hurt the party?"

107.speaker: Lucian Galade
107.text: "Even Soll knew he had to leave, but we will leave it to the President to decide."

108.speaker: Lucian Galade
108.text: "This is regarding the appointment of ministers. Currently, the President is free to appoint anyone from the members of the Assembly. Nobody else is involved with the process."

109.speaker: Player
109.text: "I will take my time and seriously consider the options before settling on one."

110.speaker: Player
110.text: "Yes, he did. But it took a long time."

111.speaker: Nia Morgna
111.text: "Some reformists suggested that the Assembly should nominate the ministers before the President approves them."

112.speaker: Nia Morgna
112.text: "There is definitely a demand to involve the Assembly in the process."

114.speaker: Player
114.text: "I agree. People should be able to elect the same person if they want to."

115.speaker: Lucian Galade
115.text: "The fifth section is about our infamous electoral threshold. Most reformists want to lower the threshold as much as possible."

116.speaker: Player
116.text: "I don't think presidential decrees need any reforms."

117.speaker: Petr Vectern
117.text: "Hey, if people keep electing one person, that means they really are content. The masses are scared of change."

118.speaker: Nia Morgna
118.text: "We can't allow somebody like Soll holding unto his seat for two decades again. We should establish limits."

119.speaker: Player
119.text: "I agree. We should involve the Assembly more in the process."

121.speaker: Lucian Galade
121.text: "They want us to include previously non-existing term limits."

123.speaker: Lucian Galade
123.text: "Yes. Tarquin Soll governed for twenty years. It seems his magic is slowly vanishing from the minds of the people, for they believe term limits are necessary."

124.speaker: Lucian Galade
124.text: "I hope it works out, Mr. President."

125.speaker: Lucian Galade
125.text: "I agree, we could keep that in."

126.speaker: Lucian Galade
126.text: "I know it is a delicate matter, sir. But you still have time to think about these."

127.speaker: Nia Morgna
127.text: "I agree. We can't allow somebody like Soll holding unto his seat for two decades again."

128.speaker: Petr Vectern
128.text: "We could also make it dependent on an enabling act from the Assembly. Sure, it would make the whole process longer but as long as we have a majority, nothing really changes."

129.speaker: Lucian Galade
129.text: "Me neither. I think it's important that the President can act quickly on matters of national importance."

132.speaker: Player
132.text: "I don't aim to leave any time soon. We keep the unlimited terms."

135.speaker: Nia Morgna
135.text: "Maybe. But Mr. Ricter doesn't think so."

136.speaker: Petr Vectern
136.text: "Yes, but this is a delicate matter. The party, and I mean, not even Albin wants us to change the threshold. They think that... this would destroy our party in the long term."

138.speaker: Petr Vectern
138.text: "Mr. Clavin and our party's reformist wing has no problems with the current law. I'm sure PFJP can be persuaded too."

139.speaker: Lucian Galade
139.text: "Not wrong. The ten percent threshold is what that allowed us to control half of the Assembly with around one third of the majority in the elections."

140.speaker: Petr Vectern
140.text: "I'm sure the reformists would completely support that."

141.speaker: Petr Vectern
141.text: "Of course, according to the ratio of the party's in government. In our case, it's only us."

142.speaker: Petr Vectern
142.text: "Frens will probably demand that we remove them completely. But he forgets that Sordland is a Presidential Republic."

143.speaker: Narrator
143.text: Lucian continued with the next section.

144.speaker: Petr Vectern
144.text: "If the entire package is to their liking, I don't think Frens will resist his own. He wouldn't say no to such major changes just because of a few small details."

145.speaker: Petr Vectern
145.text: "Sure. You'll have a long time before we start writing the final proposal together."

147.speaker: Player
147.text: “Can we go over each of the points that are in discussion for the draft?”

148.speaker: Lucian Galade
148.text: "Well, apart from the first two sections of decreasing the Supreme Court's authority and limiting the presidential vetoes... Nothing else has been agreed on unanimously."

150.speaker: Player
150.text: “I thank you all for your input.”

151.speaker: Narrator
151.text: After placing the committee's report and my own notes in front of me, I buried myself in the papers.

153.speaker: Narrator
153.text: She paused before taking my coat. It looked like she had something on her mind.

154.speaker: Livia Suno
154.text: "Mr. Rayne -- can you give me a hint about your reform plans? If you ask me, taking away the judges' immunity is long overdue, but it might anger a lot of people in these halls..."

156.speaker: Livia Suno
156.text: "I hope you'll keep me informed. I'll take your coat now."
